source_context_translations.translation: The Way that can be spoken is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
Without name, it is the beginning of Heaven and earth; with name, it is the mother of the myriad things.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A physical route or track along which one travels.
Sentence Translations (English): When he went out, he followed the road.
There is a narrow path ahead that leads to the village.
He lost his way and did not turn back.
The cart travels on the road and does not enter the fields.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A means, procedure, or course of action used to achieve something.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Often stresses an established or effective course rather than a mere plan.
Sentence Translations (English): There is a proper method for governing the state.
A learner values finding the right method.
In warfare, the method most prized is swift decision.
In all matters, if one gets the method right, then success follows.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To say, state, explain, or teach something in words.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Verbal sense distinct from the noun; often formal and declarative.
Sentence Translations (English): The teacher explains it, and the disciples listen.
The father instructed his son in righteousness.
The worthy man does not lightly speak of another's faults.
When the gentleman sees something, he must explain the principle.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The fundamental principle, path, or ordering reality being spoken of in this text.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it refers to the ineffable, ultimate Way rather than any ordinary path or method.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates that something is suitable, deserving, or deserving approval.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Evaluative rather than modal; it judges suitability or merit.
Sentence Translations (English): This policy is workable.
His words are worth listening to.
Since people's hearts are not settled, one cannot act rashly.
This rite can be practiced for a long time.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To agree to, allow, or give approval for something.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This is an active granting of approval, not mere possibility.
Sentence Translations (English): The king approved his request.
I do not dare decide on my own; I await the lord's approval.
When the assembly's discussion was settled, the matter was approved.
If the parents do not consent, the son does not proceed.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Expresses ability, possibility, or permission before a verb.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Marks possibility or capability rather than obligation.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates that a person, statement, or action is in error or not right.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Judges correctness or propriety, not simple negation.
Sentence Translations (English): Right and wrong have not yet been distinguished; the voices of the crowd are chaotic.
His words are very wrong.
To know one's error and correct it is still not too late.
A small fault does not matter; it is not a great offense.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To blame, condemn, or object to someone or something.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): An act of censure or objection, not simple negation.
Sentence Translations (English): Everyone disapproved of him.
People of the time criticized his government.
The gentleman does not condemn others recklessly.
When he heard of the mistake, he strongly criticized it.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Negates a predicate or quality; it states that something is not so.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this text it negates the following predicate phrase rather than forming the later fixed word 非常.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The enduring, unchanging Way as opposed to what is temporary or variable.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Names the Way as permanent and reliable, not a transient course.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To give something a name or designate it by a term.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): An active act of naming or calling by name.
Sentence Translations (English): The master named it.
I do not dare name it carelessly.
That mountain is what ancient times named.
Please give this thing a good name.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): The esteem or public standing a person has among others.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Concerns social standing and renown, not linguistic naming.
Sentence Translations (English): A gentleman values his reputation.
His pure conduct was widely known, and his fame reached the four quarters.
Once one's reputation is lost, it is hard to restore.
The gentleman values substance, not empty fame.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A word or designation by which something is called or identified.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Refers to naming as linguistic designation, not reputation in this passage.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A fixed, enduring designation, opposed to a shifting or temporary one.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Stresses permanence in naming rather than the act of naming itself.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Abstract absence or nonexistence treated as a substantive concept.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Used as a conceptual noun in philosophical discourse.
Sentence Translations (English): Being and nonbeing generate one another.
The sage dwells in nonbeing.
He observes its subtlety in nonbeing.
The myriad things return to nothingness.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Denies the presence, possession, or existence of what follows.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In this context it marks absence rather than philosophical 'nothingness'.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in Wang Bi recension

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The totality of the natural world, expressed by the paired terms heaven and earth.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A fixed binomial naming the whole cosmic order, not two separately emphasized items here.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): A third-person pronoun referring back to a previously mentioned person or thing.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Refers anaphorically to a known antecedent.
Sentence Translations (English): Seeing it, he was pleased.
He knows it and does not speak of it.
I love it.
Seek it and do not obtain it.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates movement or direction toward a place, person, or goal.
Sentence Translations (English): Go to the eastern suburbs.
He rode the boat toward the river.
He will go to the state gate.
From here to there.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Links a noun to the following noun to show possession, relation, or attribution.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): A grammatical connector, not a lexical noun or verb in this passage.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To cause or come into the first stage of an action, process, or state.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Marks the onset of an activity or condition.
Sentence Translations (English): Spring begins to become warm.
The army begins to move.
The affair has not yet begun.
When the day was already late, only then did he begin to return.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The point from which something starts or first comes into being.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Names the inception point or source, not the act of beginning.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text in Wang Bi recension
